LOCAL_OPTIONS.why: Report 1 develops four providers to the same depth — price, what it buys, class days and times, certifications, method kit, and the blockers (class FULL, no make-up classes, vaccine proof, food-free method, e-collar) — while Report 2's alternatives to Orion are single table rows with no credentials and, for Lori Hamilton, no way to even contact her.

FOUR_WEEK_PLAN.why: Both weeks-plans are executable and both carry advance criteria, but Report 1 spells out the drill mechanics (click on engage, feed on the turn-back, back off if he fixates past 5 seconds, move 1–5 steps not yards) and its markers are countable in feet, reps and number of dogs — Report 2 wins back some ground only by explicitly slotting work into weekday evenings and one weekend session.

DECISION.why: Both give the same unambiguous do-both verdict with dog-specific reasoning, but Report 1's flip rule is checkable against a date — six triggers including a four-week no-movement checkpoint tied to the plan itself — rather than three severity triggers only.

DENSITY.why: Report 2 is table-first and matter-of-fact end to end with a next-moves block that even time-boxes each step, while Report 1 pays for its extra detail with a ten-item mistakes list that restates the week-plan, long verbatim source quotes, and a stress-free-walks sign-off.

GROUNDING.why: Report 2's headline prices confirm against the provider pages four times over, whereas none of Report 1's figures were independently confirmed and it tells him to phone for a reactive-class price that is in fact published.

OVERALL.why: Report 1 gives you four local options you could actually choose between — credentials, method, class times, and why two are wrong for a barking dog — plus a week-by-week with countable advance markers; Report 2 reads faster and its prices check out, but if you don't like Orion its alternatives are too thin to act on.
